detail.body:
## Overview

Two decode-time fastpaths for DeepSeek-V4.x block32 MXFP8 linears on MI355X (gfx950): fuse the tiny-M activation quant into the block32 GEMM (one launch instead of two), and guard the lm_head skinny-GEMM dispatch by weight size (weights far larger than L2 stay on the generic GEMM fall-through).

Part of the DSV4.1-Flash MI355X serving fastpath series — four **independent** PRs on `main`@90c4a1a73e, each reviewable and mergeable separately, in any order. Siblings: #63180 (fused shared experts), #63181 (fused draft sampling), #63182 (draft-prepare fastpaths). The four series PRs all register kill switches in `vllm/envs.py` at the same anchor and therefore conflict textually with each other there; the resolution is to keep both sides. This branch trial-merges cleanly into current `main`.

## Claims

- **Fused quant+GEMM** (`rocm_block32_gemm.py`): at M ≤ 8 (decode shapes) the block32 linear path launched `_mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel` solely to produce the e4m3 tiles + E8M0 scales the packed GEMM immediately re-reads. The fused kernel computes that quant inside the GEMM's K loop, in registers, with the same arithmetic — one launch instead of two, no activation round trip. Bit-exact against the stock two-launch path at all eligible shapes (tuned tiers, masked K tail, in-launch split-K); ineligible inputs (non-contiguous x, fp32 x, M > 8) fall back bit-identically. Kill switch `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_FUSED_MXFP8_QUANT_GEMM`.
- **lm_head skinny-GEMM guard** (`layers/utils.py`): `wvSplitK_hf_sml` re-reads the weight matrix once per K-shard, so its effective bandwidth collapses on weights far larger than L2 — at TP=4 the DSpark draft vocab-parallel lm_head shard ([32320, 5120] bf16, ~315 MiB, one call per decode step) hit this collapse. Weights above `VLLM_SKINNY_GEMM_MAX_WEIGHT_BYTES` (default 256 MiB) stay on the generic hipBLASLt fall-through at 1 < n ≤ 5; n = 1 (no pathology) is unchanged. Kill switch `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_LMHEAD_SKINNY_GEMM_GUARD`.
- **−117 µs median decode ITL (−2.1%) on the current base** (`main`@`717cf84342`) — official DSV4.1-Flash serving command at TP=4 on MI355X, every paired run faster (rebase re-check under Validation). The submission-base study measured **−2.45% (−177/−188 µs)** over 12 position-balanced A/B cycles, and the win holds at the same magnitude across bases and images (−127 µs on the nightly ROCm-10 re-verification, −117 µs on the rebased tip). TTFT unchanged within noise.

## Validation

**Benchmark** — official serving command (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, DSpark k=5, `--monokernel`, MI355X), measured at TP=4; both fastpaths key on batch/weight shapes, not TP size. Both arms run this branch's tip; the OFF arm disables only this PR's two levers. 12 position-balanced A/B cycles (blocked AAA BBB, then BAB, then ABA), fresh server per arm per cycle, 2 sampled + 1 greedy client run per cycle (16 prompts, ISL 16 / OSL 2048, concurrency 1); arm statistic = median of per-run mean ITL; every lever's engagement asserted from the server log before the client runs.

| metric | ON median | OFF median | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| ITL t>0 | 7.065 ms | 7.243 ms | −177 µs (−2.45%) |
| ITL t0 | 6.977 ms | 7.165 ms | −188 µs |
| TTFT t>0 | 24.70 ms | 25.01 ms | −0.31 ms |
| TTFT t0 | 24.74 ms | 25.68 ms | −0.94 ms |

11 of 12 sampled cycles faster (one boundary overlap: ON max 7.148 ms vs OFF min 7.120 ms).

**Nightly ROCm-10 re-verification** — re-measured on the current nightly ROCm-10 image (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly, TP=4, same command and protocol; one fresh boot per arm, 2 sampled + 1 greedy run each): ON 5.498 ms vs OFF 5.625 ms median mean-ITL → **−127 µs (−2.27%)**, fully disjoint per-run ranges (ON 5.438–5.510, OFF 5.550–5.636), spec-decode acceptance parity (sampled-run means 3.29 vs 3.34).

**Rebase re-check** — rebased onto the latest `main`; the runtime diff is unchanged, with one added test-only commit hardening the skinny-GEMM guard tests against dropped ROCTracer captures (the profiler flake behind the `amd-mi300-model-executor` CI failure). Full local CI-equivalent suites on this tip: model_executor 1313 passed, benchmarks 219 passed. Same A/B protocol: ON 5.510 ms vs OFF 5.627 ms median mean-ITL → **−117 µs (−2.09%)**; every paired run is faster (sampled −133/−92 µs, greedy −169 µs), and both arms' censuses assert the fused path engaged / disabled respectively.

**Accuracy** — gsm8k, 5-shot, strict match, 1319 samples, one run per arm: ON 0.9325, OFF 0.9242. Both inside the 0.9196–0.9340 band observed across repeated draws of this build; across the series the paired on/off deltas scatter on both sides of zero (engine run-to-run scatter) and no arm falls outside the band.

**Tests** — the fused-quant tests live in `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py` next to the other `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel` tests (the standalone file from the first revision is gone). Beyond the bit-exactness-vs-stock comparison, the serving-shape test now also checks the fused output against a high-precision QDQ reference — dequantize both MXFP8 operands and contract in fp32, independent of the block32 GEMM kernel under test (rel err < 5e-3) — so a regression in the GEMM itself cannot hide behind the bit-exact comparison. All tests pass locally on MI355X (gfx950):

```
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp8_linear.py \
       tests/model_executor/layers/test_lmhead_skinny_gemm_guard.py -q
111 passed, 15 warnings in 47.26s
```

Of the 111, the tests added by this PR are 28 items — 21 fused-quant tests (~1.8 s) and 7 skinny-GEMM-guard tests (~1.4 s); the rest of the wall time is interpreter/import startup and the pre-existing MXFP8 suite. Single MI355X GPU, nightly ROCm-10 image.

CI notes: the fused-quant tests are CDNA4-gated (`current_platform.is_rocm() and supports_mx()`) and skip on MI300 CI pools — they are validated locally above; the skinny-GEMM guard test runs on any ROCm GPU (needs the `wvSplitK` custom op). The full pre-commit suite passes on the changed files (ruff, typos, mypy, check-torch-cuda-call, check-test-tethering, check-forbidden-imports, ...), and every commit is DCO-signed.

The tip adds review-driven changes over the benchmarked tree — tests centralized into the existing file, the QDQ reference, the kill switches renamed to `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_*`, and the long docstrings trimmed to the dispatch rules (benchmark details now in this description) — plus two earlier lint-level fixes (`torch.accelerator.synchronize()` for pre-commit `check-torch-cuda-call`, a local `args: tuple` annotation in `rocm_block32_gemm.py` for mypy). No serving-path semantics change: the renamed kill switches are the only env-facing difference.

<details><summary>Reproduction</summary>

Server (ON arm) — official serving command, as measured at TP=4 (the fastpaths are not TP=4-specific):

```
VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=1 AITER_TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR \
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 \
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 --port 8123 \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --moe-backend aiter \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true}' \
  --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \
  --block-size 128 --monokernel \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block","enable_adaptive_verification":false}'
```

OFF arm: identical, plus `VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_FUSED_MXFP8_QUANT_GEMM=1 VLLM_DEBUG_DISABLE_LMHEAD_SKINNY_GEMM_GUARD=1`.

Load (after a 4-prompt warmup; add `--temperature 0` for the greedy run):

```
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 \
  --port 8123 --backend openai --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 16 --random-output-len 2048 \
  --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1 --ignore-eos \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 90,95,99 \
  --save-result
```

Accuracy (same engine config; `max_model_len 16384` and no `cpu_offload` are the only harness deviations):

```
python -c '
import lm_eval
lm_eval.simple_evaluate(
    model="vllm",
    model_args=dict(
        pretrained="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017",
        max_model_len=16384, tensor_parallel_size=4,
        tokenizer_mode="deepseek_v41", gpu_memory_utilization=0.9,
        block_size=128, moe_backend="aiter", monokernel=True,
        attention_config={"indexer_kv_dtype": "mxfp4",
                          "indexer_sparse_logits": True},
        compilation_config={"cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 6, 8]},
        speculative_config={"method": "dspark",
                            "num_speculative_tokens": 5,
                            "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic",
                            "rejection_sample_method": "block",
                            "enable_adaptive_verification": False}),
    tasks=["gsm8k"], num_fewshot=5, batch_size=8)'
```

</details>

## Details

**Fused quant+GEMM.** At M ≤ 8 the block32 linear path pays a full `_mxfp8_quant_triton_kernel` launch just to produce the e4m3 tiles + E8M0 scales the packed GEMM immediately re-reads; the fused kernel computes that quant inside the GEMM's K loop, in registers, with the exact same arithmetic. Eligibility is a shape-table hit (serving shapes at TP=4 covering the K-structure variety: multi-band K=5120 with the in-launch split-K tier, the masked-K-tail K=1280, a small-K tile, and the default-config tier); degenerate activation blocks (all-zero, denormal, huge, negative-mirror) quantize identically, and CUDA-graph capture/replay is bit-exact in both counter states. The per-row-scale dispatch branch of the linear kernel is unaffected.

**lm_head skinny-GEMM guard.** The guard is a byte-size predicate on the weight at the skinny dispatch site: above the cap, at 1 < n ≤ 5, the call goes to the generic hipBLASLt GEMM (the same kernel class the n=6 path uses); below the cap, or at n=1, or with the kill switch, dispatch is stock. The swap is not bit-exact (different GEMM kernel, different accumulation order) — numerics are checked within bf16 GEMM tolerance, and the decision table, dispatch selection, env behavior and one-shot-per-site census warning are pinned by tests.

Both paths log their engagement as WARNINGs (one line per site/state), so ON/OFF arms can be asserted from the server log before benchmarking.

<details><summary>MI355X measurements behind the skinny-GEMM guard</summary>

Measured on MI355X (gfx950), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP=4, vocab-parallel `[32320, K]` bf16 lm_head shards, from serving traces and isolated microbenches:

- The DSpark draft lm_head `[32320, 5120]` (315.5 MiB, n=5, once per decode step) ran `wvSplitK_hf_sml<..., 2, 5>` at **1.55 TB/s** (213.8 µs/call in-graph), while the generic fall-through class runs the same GEMM at **~6.5 TB/s** (~51–73 µs).
- The n=6 target-verify lm_head `[32320, 7168]` (442 MiB) already dispatches to hipBLASLt `Cijk MT64x16x512` (56.2 µs/call in-graph, 7.9 TB/s), i.e. the fall-through kernel is fast and CUDA-graph-capture-safe in this exact serving configuration.
- Isolated microbench on the target-shape shard at n=5: wvSplitK 313.3 µs vs `torch.linear` 71.2 µs (4.4×).
- The n=1 variant (`wvSplitK_hf_sml<..., 2, 1>`) shows no pathology on large weights (6.9 TB/s on the 442 MiB shard); its fall-through (LLMM1) would be a numerics change with no speed win, so n=1 keeps stock dispatch.

The mechanism is weight re-reads: `wvSplitK_hf_sml` streams the weight once per K-shard, so above L2-sized weights the effective bandwidth collapses. This is orthogonal to VGPR-spill fixes in the skinny kernel itself (#63015, #62846) — see the related-PRs note below.

</details>

**Related PRs.**

- #63015 / #62846 (skinny-GEMM tile/spill fixes): the guard here addresses a different mechanism — weight re-reads vs L2 bandwidth on very large weights — not VGPR spills, so the two are orthogonal and compose. The spill fixes should recover `wvSplitK` throughput on shapes that spill; the re-read cost on weights far above L2 remains. Once either lands we can re-measure the `[32320, 5120]` n=5 shard on top of it and revisit the guard's byte cap / n-window if the fixed `wvSplitK` wins there.
- #59782 (fused MXFP8 quant, draft): same fused-quant idea, per-shape cutoffs and keeps the fusion past M=8 on some shapes, where this PR caps every shape at M=8 with a bit-exactness contract against the stock path. In our measurements the fusion works well at M ≤ 8; we have not measured beyond that and are happy to coordinate on which approach to keep.

+``rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm_quant`` (at M <= 8 the activation quant runs inside

 import pytest

+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.mxfp8.Mxfp8LinearKernel import (  # noqa: E402

+)
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.mxfp8.rocm_block32_gemm import (  # noqa: E402
+    rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm,
+    rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm_quant,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.mxfp8.rocm_native import (  # noqa: E402
+    RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel,
+)
+
 # (name, N, K) for the DeepSeek V4.1 attention linears at tensor_parallel=4:
 # fused wq_a|wkv is replicated, wq_b/wo_a are column-parallel, wo_b is
 # row-parallel (so K, not N, is sharded).
@@ -284,3 +302,205 @@ def test_rocm_mxfp8_quantizer_matches_torch_on_degenerate_blocks(num_rows):
     torch.testing.assert_close(
         q_triton.view(torch.uint8), q_torch.view(torch.uint8), rtol=0, atol=0
     )
+
+
+# --- tiny-M fused quant+GEMM (rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm_quant) -----------------
+#
+# Serving block32 linears at TP=4 that hit the fused path at decode,
+# covering the K-structure variety: the multi-band K=5120 shape with the
+# in-launch split-K tier (shared_gate_up), a second K=5120 tier, the
+# masked-K-tail K=1280 (EVEN_K=False), a small-K tile, and a draft-model
+# shape absent from the tuned table (_default_config tile).
+FUSED_QUANT_SERVING_SHAPES = [
+    ("shared_gate_up_tp4", 1152, 5120),
+    ("fused_wqa_wkv", 1792, 5120),
+    ("wq_b_tp4", 8192, 1280),
+    ("shared_down_tp4", 5120, 576),
+    ("default_config", 1024, 2048),
+]
+
+# Decode single, the DSpark k=5 hot M, and the M <= 8 tier bound.
+FUSED_QUANT_MS = [1, 5, 8]
+
+
+def _make_block32_weight(n: int, k: int, device: str, seed: int = 0):
+    """e4m3 weight [n, k] with compact [n//32, k//32] E8M0 block scales."""
+    torch.manual_seed(seed)
+    blocks = (torch.randn(n, k, device=device) * 0.05).view(n // 32, 32, k // 32, 32)
+    amax = blocks.abs().amax(dim=(1, 3)).clamp(min=torch.finfo(torch.float32).tiny)
+    bits = (torch.ceil(torch.log2(amax / 448.0)) + 127.0).clamp(0, 254)
+    weight = (blocks * torch.exp2(127.0 - bits)[:, None, :, None]).view(n, k)
+    return (
+        weight.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).contiguous(),
+        bits.to(torch.uint8).contiguous(),
+    )
+
+
+def _stock(x, weight, weight_scale, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16):
+    """The pre-fusion two-launch path, verbatim."""
+    x_q, x_scale = mxfp8_e4m3_quantize(x)
+    return rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm(x_q, x_scale, weight, weight_scale, out_dtype)
+
+
+def _fused_quant_hit(m, n, k) -> bool:
+    from vllm.model_executor.kernels.linear.mxfp8 import rocm_block32_gemm as g
+
+    return (m, n, k) in g._FUSED_QUANT_HIT_SHAPES
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("name,n,k", FUSED_QUANT_SERVING_SHAPES, ids=lambda v: str(v))
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("m", FUSED_QUANT_MS)
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_rocm_mxfp8_fused_quant_bit_exact_serving_shapes(name, n, k, m):
+    """The fused output equals the stock two-launch path byte-for-byte at the
+    serving shapes, and a high-precision QDQ fp32 reference within tolerance.
+
+    The reference quantizes the activation with the same quantizer and then
+    dequantizes both operands and contracts in fp32, so it is independent of
+    the block32 GEMM kernel under test.
+    """
+    torch.manual_seed(m)
+    weight, weight_scale = _make_block32_weight(n, k, "cuda")
+    x = torch.randn(m, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.5
+
+    expected = _stock(x, weight, weight_scale)
+    out = rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm_quant(x, weight, weight_scale, torch.bfloat16)
+    out2 = rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm_quant(x, weight, weight_scale, torch.bfloat16)
+
+    assert _fused_quant_hit(m, n, k), f"{name}: fused fastpath did not engage at M={m}"
+    assert torch.equal(out, expected), f"{name}: fused output differs from stock"
+    assert torch.equal(out, out2), f"{name}: fused output not deterministic"
+
+    x_q, x_scale = mxfp8_e4m3_quantize(x)
+    row_scale = weight_scale.repeat_interleave(32, dim=0)
+    reference = (
+        dequant_mxfp8_to_bf16(x_q, x_scale).float()
+        @ dequant_mxfp8_to_bf16(weight, row_scale).float().T
+    )
+    rel = (out.float() - reference).norm() / reference.norm()
+    assert rel < 5e-3, f"{name}: fused output vs QDQ reference, rel err {rel:.4f}"
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_rocm_mxfp8_fused_quant_bit_exact_degenerate_blocks():
+    """All-zero / denormal / huge / negative blocks quantize identically.
+
+    An all-zero 32-block clamps the E8M0 scale to byte 0 (2**-127,
+    subnormal in fp32): the reciprocal-form rescale must keep it NaN-free,
+    exactly as the separate quantizer does.
+    """
+    n, k, m = 512, 1024, 6
+    weight, weight_scale = _make_block32_weight(n, k, "cuda", seed=7)
+    x = torch.randn(m, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.5
+    x[0] = 0.0  # all-zero row
+    x[1, :32] = 0.0  # single zero block
+    x[1, 32:64] = 1e-38  # denormal block
+    x[2] = 3.0e30  # huge: scale byte clamps at 254
+    x[3] = -x[3]  # negative mirror
+    x[4, ::32] = 0.0  # zero at every block start
+
+    expected = _stock(x, weight, weight_scale)
+    out = rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm_quant(x, weight, weight_scale, torch.bfloat16)
+    assert _fused_quant_hit(m, n, k)
+    assert torch.isfinite(out.float()).all(), "non-finite fused output"
+    assert torch.equal(out, expected), "degenerate blocks differ from stock"
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_rocm_mxfp8_fused_quant_fallbacks_match_stock():
+    """Ineligible inputs take the internal stock path, bit-identical."""
+    n, k = 1024, 512
+    weight, weight_scale = _make_block32_weight(n, k, "cuda", seed=11)
+
+    # Non-contiguous bf16 x (stride-2 view).
+    base = torch.randn(6, 2 * k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.5
+    x_nc = base[:, ::2]
+    assert not x_nc.is_contiguous()
+    out = rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm_quant(x_nc, weight, weight_scale, torch.bfloat16)
+    assert not _fused_quant_hit(6, n, k), (
+        "non-contiguous x must not take the fused path"
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(out, _stock(x_nc.contiguous(), weight, weight_scale))
+
+    # fp32 x falls back (quantizer loads any float dtype, fused does not).
+    x_f32 = torch.randn(6, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) * 0.5
+    out = rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm_quant(x_f32, weight, weight_scale, torch.float32)
+    assert not _fused_quant_hit(6, n, k), "fp32 x must not take the fused path"
+    assert torch.equal(out, _stock(x_f32, weight, weight_scale, torch.float32))
+
+    # M > 8 (prefill-class) falls back.
+    x_big = torch.randn(16, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.5
+    out = rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm_quant(x_big, weight, weight_scale, torch.bfloat16)
+    assert not _fused_quant_hit(16, n, k), "M=16 must not take the fused path"
+    assert torch.equal(out, _stock(x_big, weight, weight_scale))
+
+    # M = 0 returns an empty output.
+    x0 = torch.randn(0, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    out = rocm_mxfp8_block32_gemm_quant(x0, weight, weight_scale, torch.bfloat16)
+    assert out.shape == (0, n)
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_rocm_mxfp8_fused_quant_per_row_scale_unaffected():
+    """Regression guard: the per-row-scale branch of
+    RocDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel.apply_weights (weight_scale [N, K//32],
+    NOT compacted to block32) must keep working when the block32 branch
+    dispatches to the fused op. The numerics of this branch are owned by
+    test_rocm_mxfp8_linear_matches_dequant_reference above; this test pins
+    the dispatch interaction only.
+    """
+    n, k, m = 1152, 5120, 7
+    torch.manual_seed(23)
+    weight_bf16 = torch.randn(n, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.05
+    weight, weight_scale = _mxfp8_e4m3_quantize_torch(weight_bf16)
+    assert weight_scale.shape == (n, k // 32), "expected per-row scales"
+
+    layer = torch.nn.Module()
+    layer.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(weight, requires_grad=False)
+    layer.weight_scale = torch.nn.Parameter(weight_scale, requires_grad=False)

+"""lm_head skinny-GEMM weight-size guard: core contracts.

+weight, so past the last-level (memory-side) cache its effective
+bandwidth collapses. At the DSV4.1-Flash TP=4 serving point the draft
+vocab-parallel lm_head shard ([32320, 5120] bf16, ~315 MiB, one call per
+decode step) hit this collapse. The guard keeps every weight above
+VLLM_SKINNY_GEMM_MAX_WEIGHT_BYTES on the generic GEMM fall-through at
+0 < n <= 5; the default cap is the memory-side cache size, read once
+from the hardware (256 MiB on MI355X, 128 MiB on MI300X-class parts),
+with a 256 MiB fallback where that cannot be read. The swap is NOT
+bit-exact (different GEMM kernel, different accumulation order) -- these
+tests check the decision table, dispatch selection, cap tuning and

+def _launched_kernels(fn, iters=3, attempts=3):
+    """Kernel names recorded for fn(), retrying failed captures.

+    Mid-suite, the ROCm activity tracer can drop every kernel record of a
+    capture while the neighboring captures in the same test stay healthy

+    produced duplicate flow start" warning). A GEMM always launches
+    device kernels, so a capture without any kernel record is a failed

+    """

+    fn()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()

Good question — the mechanisms are orthogonal. #63015/#62846 fix VGPR spills
in the skinny kernel (keeping YTILE 2); this guard addresses the weight
